source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains both kingdoms and the full dated succession without collapsing the unequal reign lists.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the troubling repeated sexual metaphor and the children within the command; leaves the woman's prior circumstances unspecified.
verses.before: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a sexually unfaithful wife and have children born from unfaithfulness, for the land commits great sexual unfaithfulness by forsaking the LORD."
verses.after: When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD told him, “Go, take a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, because the land has prostituted itself, turning away from the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of whoredom and have children of whoredom, for the land commits great whoredom by forsaking the LORD."

verses.rationale: Preserves the explicit “to him,” absent from the following births, without drawing a paternity inference.
verses.before: So he went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.after: So he went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim. She conceived and bore him a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

verses.rationale: Makes the bloodguilt concrete while keeping the dynasty and kingdom distinct.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel; for in a little while, I will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will bring an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
verses.after: The LORD told him, “Name him Jezreel. In a little while I will call the house of Jehu to account for the bloodshed at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel; for in a little while, I will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will bring an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the bow as an image of military strength and the repeated place-name.
verses.before: On that day, I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.after: On that day I will break Israel’s bow in the Valley of Jezreel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."

verses.rationale: Takes the difficult final bearing-away clause as refusal of pardon in the preceding negative scope; records its alternative in the note.
verses.before: She conceived again and bore a daughter. Then the LORD said to him, "Name her Lo-ruhama, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, to forgive them at all.
verses.after: She conceived again and bore a daughter. He told Hosea, “Name her Lo-ruhamah, because I will no longer show compassion to the house of Israel. I will certainly not forgive them.
verses.tsw_comparator: She conceived again and bore a daughter. Then the LORD said to him, "Name her Lo-ruhama, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, to forgive them at all.

verses.rationale: Preserves the third-person divine name within God's speech and every rejected military means.
verses.before: Yet I will have mercy on the house of Judah; I will save them by the LORD their God, not by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen."
verses.after: But I will show compassion to the house of Judah and save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I will have mercy on the house of Judah; I will save them by the LORD their God, not by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen."

verses.rationale: Keeps the birth sequence and weaning interval without supplying a father.
verses.before: When she had weaned Lo-ruhama, she conceived and bore a son.
verses.after: After she weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: When she had weaned Lo-ruhama, she conceived and bore a son.

verses.rationale: Preserves the open “I will not be for you” instead of adding “your God” to the verse.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not my people and I am not your God."
verses.after: He said, “Name him Lo-ammi, because you are not my people, and I will not be yours.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not my people and I am not your God."

verses.rationale: Marks the abrupt reversal with yet; retains the place, sand, and children images across the Hebrew chapter boundary.
verses.before: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."
verses.after: Yet the people of Israel will be as numerous as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where they were told, “You are not my people,” they will be called “children of the living God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it shall be said to them, "Children of the living God."

verses.rationale: Keeps coming up from the land unresolved rather than importing a particular exile; retains the Jezreel reversal.
verses.before: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint one leader and will come up from the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
verses.after: The people of Judah and Israel will gather together and appoint one leader over themselves. They will come up from the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of Judah and the people of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint one leader and shall come up from the land, for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Renders the reversed name meanings directly while preserving male and female kinship terms.
verses.before: Say to your brothers, "My people," and to your sisters, "Mercy."
verses.after: Call your brothers “My People,” and your sisters “Shown Compassion.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to your brothers, "My people," and to your sisters, "Mercy."

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated lawsuit imperative and bodily imagery rather than sanitizing the accusation.
verses.before: Plead with your mother, plead— for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband— that she put away her harlotry from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
verses.after: “Bring a case against your mother—bring a case! She is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the prostitution from her face and the adultery from between her breasts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Plead with your mother, plead— for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband— that she put away her harlotry from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,

verses.rationale: Preserves all threatened violence as the speaker's words, including killing rather than merely hardship.
verses.before: lest I strip her naked and set her as in the day of her birth, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
verses.after: Otherwise I will strip her naked and leave her as she was on the day she was born. I will make her like a wilderness, turn her into parched land, and kill her with thirst.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest I strip her naked and set her as in the day of her birth, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a dry land, and kill her with thirst.

verses.rationale: Maintains the compassion motif and the explicit extension of judgment to children.
verses.before: Upon her children I will have no mercy, for they are children of harlotry.
verses.after: I will show no compassion to her children, because they are children of prostitution.
verses.tsw_comparator: Upon her children I will have no mercy, for they are children of harlotry.

verses.rationale: Keeps her reported rationale and the paired provisions that the response will reclaim.
verses.before: For their mother has played the harlot; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who provide my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
verses.after: Their mother has prostituted herself; the woman who conceived them has acted shamefully. She said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and water, my wool and flax, my oil and drink.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For their mother has played the harlot; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who provide my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's direct-address to third-person shift rather than smoothing it invisibly.
verses.before: So, look, I will hedge up her way with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, so she cannot find her paths.
verses.after: So now I will block your road with thorns. I will wall her in so she cannot find her paths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her way with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, so she cannot find her paths.

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel failed pursuit and her pragmatic stated motive.
verses.before: She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."
verses.after: She will pursue her lovers but will not catch them; she will seek them but will not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will go back to my first husband, because I was better off then than I am now.’
verses.tsw_comparator: She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them; she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic giver and shift to plural they in the use of gold.
verses.before: And she did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the wine, and the oil, and who lavished upon her silver and gold that they used for Baal.
verses.after: She did not know that I was the one who gave her grain, new wine, and oil. I lavished silver on her, and gold that they used for Baal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the wine, and the oil, and who lavished upon her silver and gold that they used for Baal.

verses.rationale: Links the possessive reversal to the earlier provision list and preserves nakedness.
verses.before: So, I will take back my grain in its time, and my wine in its season, and will take away my wool and my flax, which were to cover her nakedness.
verses.after: So I will take back my grain when it ripens and my new wine in its season. I will reclaim my wool and flax, which were to cover her nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, I will take back my grain in its time, and my wine in its season, and will take away my wool and my flax, which were to cover her nakedness.

verses.rationale: Retains public humiliation and the hand image without euphemism.
verses.before: Now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of my hand.
verses.after: Now I will expose her shame in full view of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will deliver her out of my hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full calendar list, including Sabbaths rather than general holidays.
verses.before: I will put an end to all her mirth, her feasts, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her appointed festivals.
verses.after: I will put an end to all her rejoicing— her festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths, and all her appointed celebrations.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will put an end to all her mirth, her feasts, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her appointed festivals.

verses.rationale: Keeps wages as part of the sexual-economic metaphor and the agricultural devastation.
verses.before: I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she has said, "These are my wages, which my lovers have given me." I will make them a forest, and the beasts of the field will devour them.
verses.after: I will devastate her vines and fig trees, which she called ‘my wages, given by my lovers.’ I will turn them into a thicket, and wild animals will eat them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she has said, "These are my wages, which my lovers have given me." And I will make them a forest, and the beasts of the field will devour them.

verses.rationale: Retains plural Baals and puts the emphatic forgotten speaker at the close.
verses.before: I will punish her for the days of the Baals, to whom she burned incense and adorned herself with her ring and jewelry, and went after her lovers and forgot me, declares the LORD.
verses.after: I will call her to account for the days when she burned offerings to the Baals, adorned herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers. But me she forgot,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will punish her for the days of the Baals, to whom she burned incense and adorned herself with her ring and jewelry, and went after her lovers and forgot me, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the surprising therefore/so turn and the heart idiom, without erasing its tension after threats.
verses.before: So, look, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
verses.after: “So now I will entice her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.

verses.rationale: Uses respond for anah, with sing possible in the note; keeps Achor and the exodus comparison.
verses.before: From there I will give her vineyards, and the Valley of Achor, as a door of hope. She will respond there as in the days of her youth, as in the time she came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.after: There I will give her back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor a doorway of hope. There she will respond as in her youth, as on the day she came up from Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there I will give her vineyards, and the Valley of Achor, as a door of hope. She will respond there as in the days of her youth, as in the time she came out of the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains Baal to make the title/name wordplay teachable rather than silently using only master.
verses.before: On that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My husband," and no longer will you call me "My Baal."
verses.after: On that day,” declares the LORD, “you will call me ‘My Husband’ and no longer call me ‘My Baal.’
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My husband," and no longer will you call me "My Baal."

verses.rationale: Maintains the return to third-person and the repeated names motif.
verses.before: For I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will be remembered by name no more.
verses.after: I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth; their names will no longer be spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will be remembered by name no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps the nonhuman covenant partners and the unusual breaking of war itself.
verses.before: I will make a covenant for them on that day with the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens, and the creeping things of the ground. I will abolish the bow, the sword, and war from the land; I will make you lie down in safety.
verses.after: On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky, and the creatures that move along the ground. I will break bow, sword, and war from the land and let them lie down in safety.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make a covenant for them on that day with the beasts of the field, the birds of the heavens, and the creeping things of the ground. And I will abolish the bow, the sword, and war from the land; I will make you lie down in safety.

verses.rationale: Repeats the marriage pledge and retains all four covenant qualities rather than reducing them to affection.
verses.before: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in mercy.
verses.after: I will pledge myself to you in marriage forever. I will pledge myself to you in righteousness and justice, in faithful love and compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in mercy.

verses.rationale: Completes the threefold pledge while preserving knowledge as relationship and recognition, not adding an explanation to text.
verses.before: I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
verses.after: I will pledge myself to you in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated answer verb at the start of the responsive chain.
verses.before: On that day I will answer, declares the LORD, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
verses.after: On that day I will answer,” declares the LORD. “I will answer the skies, and they will answer the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day I will answer, declares the LORD, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the chain's final personified agricultural terms and the name that means God sows.
verses.before: The earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
verses.after: The earth will answer the grain, new wine, and oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Preserves feminine sowing then masculine response and the names' reversal rather than flattening pronouns.
verses.before: I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on "Not Pitied." I will say to "Not My People," "You are my people," and he will say, "You are my God."
verses.after: I will sow her for myself in the land. I will show compassion to Lo-ruhamah. To Lo-ammi I will say, ‘You are my people,’ and he will say, ‘My God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on "Not Pitied." I will say to "Not My People," "You are my people," and he will say, "You are my God."

verses.rationale: Follows the pointed beloved-by-a-companion reading; leaves the woman unnamed and the raisin cakes concrete.
verses.before: The LORD said to me, “Go again, love a woman loved by another and committing adultery, just as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins.”
verses.after: The LORD said to me again, “Go, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, just as the LORD loves the people of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to me, “Go again, love a woman loved by another and committing adultery, just as the LORD loves the children of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love cakes of raisins.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both ancient measures and price without inventing the legal setting of the transaction.
verses.before: So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.
verses.after: So I acquired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, a homer of barley, and a lethek of barley.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.

verses.rationale: Keeps the terse reciprocal ending open rather than asserting a fully explained sexual arrangement.
verses.before: I said to her, “You will remain with me many days. You will not prostitute yourself, and you will not belong to another man; and I also will be so toward you.”
verses.after: I told her, “You must stay with me for many days. You must not prostitute yourself or belong to another man, and I will be the same toward you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said to her, “You shall remain with me many days. You shall not prostitute yourself, and you shall not belong to another man; and I also will be so toward you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all six absent institutions and objects, without sorting them into approved and disapproved in the verse.
verses.before: For the children of Israel will remain many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or household gods.
verses.after: For many days the people of Israel will remain without king or ruler, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, without ephod or household gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the children of Israel will remain many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or household gods.

verses.rationale: Retains David as named and the combination of fear and goodness without supplying a messianic identification.
verses.before: Afterward the children of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness in the latter days.
verses.after: Afterward the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. In the days to come they will approach the LORD and his goodness with trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward the children of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness in the latter days.

verses.rationale: Introduces the legal dispute clearly and keeps the three missing qualities distinct.
verses.before: Hear the word of the LORD, children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land: “There is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land.
verses.after: Hear the word of the LORD, people of Israel! The LORD has a case against those who live in the land: there is no truthfulness, no faithful love, and no knowledge of God in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the word of the LORD, children of Israel, for the LORD has a case against the inhabitants of the land: “There is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, and no knowledge of God in the land.

verses.rationale: Maintains the catalogue and the repeated bloodshed image with an intelligible boundary idiom.
verses.before: Swearing and lying, murder and stealing and adultery break out; bloodshed touches bloodshed.
verses.after: Cursing and lying, murder and theft and adultery— they burst every boundary, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Swearing and lying, murder and stealing and adultery break out; bloodshed touches bloodshed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ecological reach of judgment, including fish and land mourning.
verses.before: So the land mourns, and everyone who lives in it languishes, with the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens; even the fish of the sea are taken away.
verses.after: That is why the land mourns and everyone who lives in it wastes away, along with the wild animals and birds of the sky. Even the fish of the sea are swept away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the land mourns, and everyone who lives in it languishes, with the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens; even the fish of the sea are taken away.

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult transmitted comparison rather than silently emending it to an accusation against priests.
verses.before: Yet let no one contend, and let no one accuse, for your people are like those who contend with a priest.
verses.after: “Yet let no one bring a case; let no one make an accusation. Your people are like those who bring a case against a priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet let no one contend, and let no one accuse, for your people are like those who contend with a priest.

verses.rationale: Retains paired day/night and the mother metaphor, leaving its collective force to a note.
verses.before: You will stumble by day, and the prophet also will stumble with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.
verses.after: You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night. I will destroy your mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will stumble by day, and the prophet also will stumble with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal rejection and forgetting, with priestly address and consequences for children explicit.
verses.before: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as priest to me. Since you forgot the instruction of your God, I also will forget your children.
verses.after: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as my priest. Because you have forgotten your God’s instruction, I too will forget your children.
verses.tsw_comparator: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as priest to me. Since you forgot the instruction of your God, I also will forget your children.

verses.rationale: Follows the first-person exchange in the pinned text rather than substituting an ancient alternative subject.
verses.before: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against me; I will exchange their glory for shame.
verses.after: The more they increased, the more they sinned against me. I will exchange their honor for disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against me; I will exchange their glory for shame.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sin/sin-offering double sense rather than resolving the exploitative image into a paraphrase.
verses.before: They feed on the sin of my people and lift up their appetite toward their guilt.
verses.after: They feed on my people’s sin and set their hearts on their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They feed on the sin of my people and lift up their appetite toward their guilt.

verses.rationale: Renders the proverbial leveling and keeps both conduct and recompense clauses.
verses.before: And it will be: like people, like priest. I will attend to them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
verses.after: It will be the same for people and priest. I will call them to account for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it will be: like people, like priest. I will attend to them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.

verses.rationale: Reads keep at the preceding clause as abandoning observance; notes the possible linkage with the next verse.
verses.before: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves but not multiply, because they have abandoned giving heed to the LORD.
verses.after: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves but not increase, because they have abandoned the LORD and ceased to keep faith with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will eat but not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves but not multiply, because they have abandoned giving heed to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three agents and renders heart as understanding in this context.
verses.before: Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away the heart.
verses.after: Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away the heart.

verses.rationale: Retains the ridicule of wooden divination and the repeated governing metaphor.
verses.before: My people inquire of their wood, and their staff gives them an answer. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray, and they prostitute themselves away from their God.
verses.after: My people consult a piece of wood; a stick tells them what to do! A spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have prostituted themselves, leaving their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: My people inquire of their wood, and their staff gives them an answer. For a spirit of prostitution leads them astray, and they prostitute themselves away from their God.

verses.rationale: Preserves tree types, stated attraction of shade, and specific family relationships.
verses.before: They sacrifice on the tops of the mountains and burn incense on the hills, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because their shade is good. So your daughters prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
verses.after: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. That is why your daughters prostitute themselves and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sacrifice on the tops of the mountains and burn incense on the hills, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because their shade is good. Therefore your daughters prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

verses.rationale: Makes the male referents explicit and avoids claiming certainty that qedeshot denotes cultic prostitution.
verses.before: I will not attend to your daughters when they prostitute themselves, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves go aside with prostitutes and sacrifice with cult prostitutes. A people without understanding will be ruined.
verses.after: I will not punish your daughters for prostitution or your daughters-in-law for adultery, for the men themselves go off with prostitutes and sacrifice with women devoted to a shrine. A people without understanding comes to ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not attend to your daughters when they prostitute themselves, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves go aside with prostitutes and sacrifice with cult prostitutes. A people without understanding will be ruined.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah's warning separate from Israel's conduct and preserves the polemical place-name.
verses.before: Though you prostitute yourself, Israel, let Judah not become guilty. Do not come to Gilgal, and do not go up to Beth-Aven, and do not swear, “As the LORD lives!”
verses.after: Though you prostitute yourself, Israel, let Judah not become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal or go up to Beth-aven. Do not swear, ‘As the LORD lives!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Though you prostitute yourself, Israel, let Judah not become guilty. Do not come to Gilgal, and do not go up to Beth-Aven, and do not swear, “As the LORD lives!”

verses.rationale: Retains the heifer/lamb contrast; marks the final clause as a contextual question with declarative alternative noted.
verses.before: For Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in a broad place?
verses.after: Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in an open meadow?
verses.tsw_comparator: For Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in a broad place?

verses.rationale: Keeps the terse command and singular collective personification.
verses.before: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone.
verses.after: Ephraim is bound to idols. Leave him alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone.

verses.rationale: Renders the difficult repeated love/give phrase cautiously while retaining the rulers' shameful desire.
verses.before: Their drink is gone; they give themselves to prostitution. Her rulers dearly love shame.
verses.after: When their drinking is over, they give themselves to prostitution. Her rulers dearly love disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their drink is gone; they give themselves to prostitution. Her rulers dearly love shame.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wind's wings and the source's singular-to-plural shift.
verses.before: A wind has wrapped her in its wings, and they will be ashamed because of their sacrifices.
verses.after: A wind has wrapped her in its wings, and they will be ashamed of their sacrifices.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A wind has wrapped her in its wings, and they will be ashamed because of their sacrifices.

verses.rationale: Maintains the three addressees and judicial/hunting images with named locations.
verses.before: Hear this, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Give ear, house of the king! For judgment is for you, because you have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.
verses.after: “Hear this, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, royal house! Judgment concerns you, for you have been a trap at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Give ear, house of the king! For judgment is for you, because you have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread over Tabor.

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult slaughter/rebels wording without an unmarked Shittim emendation.
verses.before: The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I am discipline for them all.
verses.after: The rebels have sunk deep into slaughter, but I will discipline them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I am discipline for them all.

verses.rationale: Repeats Ephraim and Israel in both balanced accusations.
verses.before: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now, Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself; Israel is defiled.
verses.after: I know Ephraim; Israel is not hidden from me. Now you have prostituted yourself, Ephraim; Israel is defiled.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now, Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself; Israel is defiled.

verses.rationale: Keeps deeds as the impediment and knowledge as the closing diagnosis.
verses.before: Their deeds do not allow them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
verses.after: Their deeds will not let them return to their God. A spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their deeds do not allow them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the witness metaphor and widening inclusion of Judah.
verses.before: The pride of Israel testifies to his face; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt; Judah also stumbles with them.
verses.after: Israel’s pride testifies against him. Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt; Judah too stumbles with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pride of Israel testifies to his face; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt; Judah also stumbles with them.

verses.rationale: Leaves sacrificial purpose implicit in the animals rather than adding it to the source.
verses.before: With their flocks and herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.
verses.after: With their flocks and herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him. He has withdrawn from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: With their flocks and herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.

verses.rationale: Retains the enigmatic devouring new moon and strange children rather than overexplaining either.
verses.before: They have acted treacherously against the LORD, for they have borne foreign children. Now a new moon will devour them with their portions.
verses.after: They have betrayed the LORD; they have borne children who are strangers. Now a new moon will devour them and their fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have acted treacherously against the LORD, for they have borne foreign children. Now a new moon will devour them with their portions.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes shofar and trumpet and retains the abrupt ambiguous final cry.
verses.before: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm at Beth-Aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
verses.after: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm in Beth-aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
verses.tsw_comparator: Blow the ram’s horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm at Beth-Aven! Behind you, Benjamin!

verses.rationale: Preserves the specified day and the assurance of the announcement.
verses.before: Ephraim will become a desolation on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I reveal what is certain.
verses.after: Ephraim will become a wasteland on the day of reckoning. Among Israel’s tribes I have announced what is certain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim will become a desolation on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I make known what is certain.

verses.rationale: Makes the boundary violation intelligible while keeping the water simile.
verses.before: The officials of Judah have become like people who move a boundary marker. Upon them I will pour out my fury like water.
verses.after: Judah’s rulers have become like those who move boundary stones. I will pour my fury over them like water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The officials of Judah have become like those who move a boundary marker. Upon them I will pour out my fury like water.

verses.rationale: Follows tsaw as command in the pinned text; flags its obscure referent rather than importing idols.
verses.before: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was determined to walk after a command.
verses.after: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was determined to follow a command.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was determined to walk after a command.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two small destructive images before the lion comparison.
verses.before: So I am like a moth to Ephraim and like decay to the house of Judah.
verses.after: I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I am like a moth to Ephraim and like decay to the house of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unusual king epithet as contending rather than inventing a personal name or silently reading great king.
verses.before: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he is not able to heal you or cure your wound.
verses.after: Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound. Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the contending king. But he cannot heal you or cure your wound.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he is not able to heal you or cure your wound.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic doubled I and the escalating predatory actions.
verses.before: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear and go away; I will carry off, and no one will rescue.
verses.after: For I am like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear and go away; I will carry off, and no one will rescue.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear and go away; I will carry off, and no one will rescue.

verses.rationale: Uses acknowledge guilt contextually for asham, retaining face and the intensified seeking.
verses.before: I will go and return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will seek me earnestly.
verses.after: I will go back to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will seek me earnestly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will go and return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will seek me earnestly.

verses.rationale: Keeps the responding communal voice and recalls the preceding lion and wound images.
verses.before: Come, let us return to the LORD, for he has torn us, but he will heal us; he has struck us, but he will bind us up.
verses.after: “Come, let us return to the LORD. He has torn us, but he will heal us; he has struck us, but he will bind our wounds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come, let us return to the LORD, for he has torn us, but he will heal us; he has struck us, but he will bind us up.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated two/third-day sequence without importing a later fulfillment into the translation.
verses.before: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
verses.after: After two days he will bring us back to life; on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.

verses.rationale: Maintains the repeated knowing and agricultural seasonal comparison.
verses.before: Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD. His going forth is as certain as dawn; he will come to us like rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.
verses.after: Let us know him; let us press on to know the LORD. His coming is as certain as the dawn. He will come to us like the rain, like spring rain watering the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us know; let us press on to know the LORD. His going forth is as certain as dawn; he will come to us like rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.

verses.rationale: Marks God's reply and repeats the question rather than merging the two addressees.
verses.before: What will I do with you, Ephraim? What will I do with you, Judah? Your steadfast love is like a morning cloud, like dew that goes away early.
verses.after: “What am I to do with you, Ephraim? What am I to do with you, Judah? Your faithful love is like a morning cloud, like dew that vanishes early.
verses.tsw_comparator: What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your steadfast love is like a morning cloud, like dew that goes away early.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent word imagery and follows the pointed your-judgments wording with contextual against you.
verses.before: So I cut them down by the prophets; I killed them by the words of my mouth, and my judgment goes out like light.
verses.after: That is why I have cut them down through the prophets, killed them with the words of my mouth. The judgments against you go out like light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I cut them down by the prophets; I killed them by the words of my mouth, and my judgment goes out like light.

verses.rationale: Keeps hesed consistent and the parallel preference statements rather than generalizing to kindness alone.
verses.before: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
verses.after: I desire faithful love, not sacrifice; knowledge of God, rather than burnt offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

verses.rationale: Retains Adam and there; notes the consequential human/place-name alternatives.
verses.before: But like Adam they transgressed the covenant; there they acted treacherously against me.
verses.after: But like Adam they broke the covenant; there they betrayed me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But like Adam they transgressed the covenant; there they acted treacherously against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps footprints suggested by the rare adjective and does not replace Gilead with another site.
verses.before: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with blood.
verses.after: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with blood.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly agency, ambush, and the directional place-name.
verses.before: As bands of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murders on the road to Shechem; surely they commit outrage.
verses.after: Like bands of raiders waiting for someone, a company of priests murders on the road to Shechem. They have committed an outrage.
verses.tsw_comparator: As bands of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murders on the road to Shechem; surely they commit outrage.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form for horror and retains the two collective names.
verses.before: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrifying thing: there Ephraim prostitutes himself; Israel is defiled.
verses.after: In the house of Israel I have seen a horror: Ephraim’s prostitution is there; Israel is defiled.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrifying thing: there Ephraim prostitutes himself; Israel is defiled.

verses.rationale: Keeps harvest undescribed and the final temporal clause open across the chapter boundary.
verses.before: For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed when I restore the fortunes of my people.
verses.after: For you too, Judah, a harvest is appointed. When I restore my people’s fortunes,
verses.tsw_comparator: For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed when I restore the fortunes of my people.

verses.rationale: Carries the previous temporal clause forward and contrasts inside theft with outside raids.
verses.before: When I would heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim is uncovered and the evil deeds of Samaria, for they practice falsehood. A thief enters, and a band raids outside.
verses.after: when I heal Israel, Ephraim’s guilt and Samaria’s evil are exposed. They practice deceit; a thief breaks in, and a raiding band plunders outside.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I would heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim is uncovered and the evil deeds of Samaria, for they practice falsehood. A thief enters, and a band raids outside.

verses.rationale: Preserves heart, surrounding deeds, and divine sight as linked images.
verses.before: But they do not say in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds surround them; they are before my face.
verses.after: They do not take it to heart that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds surround them; they are right before my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they do not say in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds surround them; they are before my face.

verses.rationale: Does not infer a specific coup beyond the stated royal pleasure in wrongdoing.
verses.before: With their evil they make the king glad, and with their lies the officials.
verses.after: Their evil makes a king glad; their lies delight rulers.
verses.tsw_comparator: With their evil they make the king glad, and with their lies the officials.

verses.rationale: Retains the baker's pause and dough process, which give the extended metaphor its pacing.
verses.before: All of them are adulterers; they are like an oven heated by a baker who stops stirring the fire from kneading the dough until it is leavened.
verses.after: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker, who stops stirring the fire from the kneading of the dough until it rises.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them are adulterers; they are like an oven heated by a baker who stops stirring the fire from kneading the dough until it is leavened.

verses.rationale: Leaves the royal occasion and hand gesture open instead of inventing an anniversary or alliance ceremony.
verses.before: On the day of our king the officials became sick with the heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scoffers.
verses.after: On the day of our king, the rulers became sick with the heat of wine. He stretched out his hand with scoffers.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day of our king the officials became sick with the heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scoffers.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned baker reading and preserves the abrupt pronoun shift in the oven image.
verses.before: For they approach with their heart like an oven in their plotting. All night their anger sleeps; in the morning it burns like a flaming fire.
verses.after: They bring their hearts near like an oven as they lie in wait. Their baker sleeps all night; in the morning it burns like a blazing fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they approach with their heart like an oven in their plotting. All night their anger sleeps; in the morning it burns like a flaming fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three all/none assertions and the transfer from heated desire to political violence.
verses.before: All of them are hot like an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings have fallen; none of them calls to me.
verses.after: All of them burn hot as an oven and consume their judges. All their kings have fallen; none of them calls to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them are hot like an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings have fallen; none of them calls to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the homely unturned bread image rather than substituting an abstract accusation.
verses.before: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples. Ephraim is a cake not turned.
verses.after: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples. Ephraim is a flatbread never turned over.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples. Ephraim is a cake not turned.

verses.rationale: Repeats the ignorance refrain exactly across strength and aging images.
verses.before: Strangers devour his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hairs are also sprinkled on him, but he does not know it.
verses.after: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hairs are scattered over him, but he does not know it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strangers devour his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hairs are also sprinkled on him, but he does not know it.

verses.rationale: Matches the recurring pride/witness phrase and retains the two failed responses.
verses.before: The pride of Israel testifies to his face, yet they do not return to the LORD their God or seek him for all this.
verses.after: Israel’s pride testifies against him, yet they have not returned to the LORD their God or sought him through all this.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pride of Israel testifies to his face, yet they do not return to the LORD their God or seek him for all this.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dove and contrasting diplomatic directions without adding treaty history.
verses.before: Ephraim has become like a dove, simple and without heart: they call to Egypt; they go to Assyria.
verses.after: Ephraim is like a gullible dove without sense. They call to Egypt; they go to Assyria.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim has become like a dove, simple and without heart: they call to Egypt; they go to Assyria.

verses.rationale: Retains the divine trap and the difficult final hearing clause with its communal reference.
verses.before: As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the heavens. I will discipline them according to the report to their congregation.
verses.after: As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the sky. I will discipline them as their congregation has been told.
verses.tsw_comparator: As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the heavens. I will discipline them according to the report to their congregation.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired lament and judgment, with the conditional desire to redeem rather than an unconditional prediction.
verses.before: Woe to them, for they have fled from me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies against me.
verses.after: Woe to them, for they have wandered away from me! Devastation to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies about me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to them, for they have fled from me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies against me.

verses.rationale: Follows transmitted gathering rather than emending to cutting themselves; retains the inner/outer contrast.
verses.before: They do not cry out to me from their heart, but they wail upon their beds. For grain and new wine they gather themselves; they turn against me.
verses.after: They do not cry to me from their hearts; they wail on their beds. They gather for grain and new wine and turn against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not cry out to me from their heart, but they wail upon their beds. For grain and new wine they gather themselves; they turn against me.

verses.rationale: Preserves both training and strengthening and the reversal of care into hostility.
verses.before: Though I trained and strengthened their arms, they devise evil against me.
verses.after: I trained them and strengthened their arms, but they plot evil against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though I trained and strengthened their arms, they devise evil against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the elliptical upward and defective bow, without forcing Most High into the consonants.
verses.before: They return, but not upward. They are like a deceptive bow. Their officials will fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongue. This will be their mockery in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: They turn, but not upward; they have become an unreliable bow. Their rulers will fall by the sword because of their raging tongues. This will make them a laughingstock in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They return, but not upward. They are like a deceptive bow. Their officials will fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongue. This will be their mockery in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Supplies only a minimal subject for the abrupt eagle clause and preserves covenant/instruction pairing.
verses.before: Put the ram’s horn to your mouth! One comes like an eagle against the house of the LORD, because they transgressed my covenant and rebelled against my instruction.
verses.after: Put the ram’s horn to your lips! Like an eagle, one comes against the house of the LORD, because they have broken my covenant and rebelled against my instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Put the ram’s horn to your mouth! One comes like an eagle against the house of the LORD, because they transgressed my covenant and rebelled against my instruction.

verses.rationale: Retains singular my alongside plural we and explicitly locates Israel within the cry.
verses.before: To me they cry, “My God, we Israel know you!”
verses.after: They cry to me, ‘My God, we in Israel know you!’
verses.tsw_comparator: To me they cry, “My God, we Israel know you!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated rejection motif and collective masculine reference.
verses.before: Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
verses.after: Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.

verses.rationale: Renders lack of knowing as lack of acknowledgment without implying divine ignorance; leaves cut-off referent broad.
verses.before: They made kings, but not from me; they made officials, but I did not know it. With their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, so that they might be cut off.
verses.after: They appointed kings without me; they set up rulers without my acknowledgment. From their silver and gold they made idols for themselves, only to be cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made kings, but not from me; they made officials, but I did not know it. With their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, so that they might be cut off.

verses.rationale: Uses a passive English clause for the uncertain subject of rejected and retains the challenging final question.
verses.before: Your calf is rejected, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
verses.after: Your calf is rejected, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
verses.tsw_comparator: Your calf is rejected, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?

verses.rationale: Keeps the maker-versus-deity argument and the concrete destruction.
verses.before: For it is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. Surely the calf of Samaria will become splinters.
verses.after: It comes from Israel: a craftsman made it; it is no god. Samaria’s calf will become splinters.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is not God. Surely the calf of Samaria will become splinters.

verses.rationale: Retains the escalating failed-harvest image and hypothetical final concession.
verses.before: For they sow wind and reap whirlwind. Standing grain has no head; it produces no flour. Even if it produced, strangers would swallow it.
verses.after: They sow wind and harvest a whirlwind. The stalk has no standing grain; the shoot produces no flour. Even if it did, foreigners would swallow it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they sow wind and reap whirlwind. Standing grain has no head; it produces no flour. Even if it produced, strangers would swallow it.

verses.rationale: Repeats swallowed to connect the previous crop to the people, preserving the unwanted vessel.
verses.before: Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a vessel in which no one delights.
verses.after: Israel has been swallowed up. Now among the nations they are a vessel no one wants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a vessel in which no one delights.

verses.rationale: Keeps the solitary animal image beside the contradictory purchasing of lovers.
verses.before: For they have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers.
verses.after: They have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey off on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers.

verses.rationale: Keeps the obscure gathering and royal burden without assigning an unstated named monarch.
verses.before: Though they hire among the nations, now I will gather them, and they will begin to diminish under the burden of king and officials.
verses.after: Though they hire among the nations, now I will gather them. They will soon begin to suffer under the burden of the king of rulers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though they hire among the nations, now I will gather them, and they will begin to diminish under the burden of king and officials.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sin/sin-offering play rather than eliminating its deliberate ambiguity.
verses.before: Because Ephraim multiplied altars for sin, altars became for him altars for sinning.
verses.after: Ephraim multiplied altars for sin; they became altars for sinning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because Ephraim multiplied altars for sin, altars became for him altars for sinning.

verses.rationale: Renders the abundance and foreignness clearly, following the written/read verbal sense without making a historical writing claim.
verses.before: Though I write for him my instruction by tens of thousands, they are regarded as something foreign.
verses.after: Were I to write my instruction for him in countless provisions, they would be regarded as something foreign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though I write for him my instruction by tens of thousands, they are regarded as something foreign.

verses.rationale: Keeps consumption, rejection, remembrance, and the explicit Egypt destination.
verses.before: As for my sacrificial gifts, they sacrifice flesh and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their guilt and attend to their sins. They will return to Egypt.
verses.after: As for my sacrificial gifts, they sacrifice meat and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their guilt and punish their sins. They will return to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for my sacrificial gifts, they sacrifice flesh and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their guilt and attend to their sins. They will return to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's shifting collective gender and distinguishes palaces and fortified cities.
verses.before: Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces, and Judah multiplied fortified cities. Yet I will send fire upon his cities, and it will devour her palaces.
verses.after: Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces; Judah multiplied fortified cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will consume her citadels.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel forgot his Maker and built palaces, and Judah multiplied fortified cities. But I will send fire upon his cities, and it will devour her palaces.

verses.rationale: Retains the sexual-economic image at agricultural sites rather than abstracting it into disloyalty.
verses.before: Do not rejoice, Israel, with exultation like the peoples, for you have prostituted yourself away from your God. You have loved a prostitute’s wages on every threshing floor.
verses.after: Do not rejoice, Israel; do not celebrate like the peoples. You have prostituted yourself, leaving your God; you have loved a prostitute’s wages on every grain-threshing floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not rejoice, Israel, with exultation like the peoples, for you have prostituted yourself away from your God. You have loved a prostitute’s wages on every threshing floor.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural-to-feminine shift and the failed expectation of produce.
verses.before: Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and new wine will fail her.
verses.after: Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them; new wine will fail her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and new wine will fail her.

verses.rationale: Preserves both named exile locations and the ritual category unclean.
verses.before: They will not remain in the land of the LORD. Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.
verses.after: They will not remain in the LORD’s land. Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not remain in the land of the LORD. Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes provision for life from admissibility at the sanctuary and retains mourning impurity.
verses.before: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. Their bread will be like the bread of mourning; everyone who eat it will become unclean. For their bread will be for their own hunger; it will not come into the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They will pour out no wine for the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. Their food will be like mourners’ bread: all who eat it will become unclean. Their bread will be only for their own hunger; it will not enter the house of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. Their bread will be like the bread of mourning; all who eat it will become unclean. For their bread will be for their own hunger; it will not come into the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the questions focused on worship's lost calendar.
verses.before: What will you do on the day of appointed festival, on the day of the feast of the LORD?
verses.after: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s festival?
verses.tsw_comparator: What will you do on the day of appointed festival, on the day of the feast of the LORD?

verses.rationale: Retains the Egypt/Memphis pairing and vegetation inheriting valuables rather than adding architectural detail.
verses.before: For look, they go away from destruction. Egypt will gather them; Memphis will bury them. Nettles will possess their precious things of silver; thorns will be in their tents.
verses.after: Look, even if they escape devastation, Egypt will gather them; Memphis will bury them. Nettles will take over their precious silver, and thorns their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, they go away from destruction. Egypt will gather them; Memphis will bury them. Nettles will possess their precious things of silver; thorns will be in their tents.

verses.rationale: Treats the charge as hostile speech while recording the unmarked-speaker alternative in notes.
verses.before: The days of visitation have come; the days of repayment have come. Israel will know it. The prophet is a fool; the man of the spirit is mad— because of the greatness of your guilt and the greatness of hostility.
verses.after: The days of reckoning have come; the days of repayment have come. Israel will know it. “The prophet is a fool; the man of the spirit is mad!” So great is your guilt, so great your hostility.
verses.tsw_comparator: The days of visitation have come; the days of repayment have come. Israel will know it. The prophet is a fool; the man of the spirit is mad— because of the greatness of your guilt and the greatness of hostility.

verses.rationale: Chooses the watchman-prophet syntax while retaining its difficult relation to Ephraim and God.
verses.before: Ephraim’s watchman is with my God; the prophet finds a fowler’s snare on all his ways, and hostility in the house of his God.
verses.after: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman with my God, yet a birdcatcher’s trap lies on all his paths, and hostility fills the house of his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim’s watchman is with my God; the prophet finds a fowler’s snare on all his ways, and hostility in the house of his God.

verses.rationale: Keeps historical allusion unnamed beyond Gibeah and repeats the judgment formula.
verses.before: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their guilt; he will attend to their sins.
verses.after: They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their guilt and punish their sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their guilt; he will attend to their sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves the delight-to-defilement reversal and the polemical name Shame.
verses.before: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your ancestors. But they came to Baal-Peor and consecrated themselves to Shame, and they became detestable like the thing they loved.
verses.after: “I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your ancestors like the first fruit on a young fig tree. But they came to Baal-peor and devoted themselves to Shame. They became as detestable as what they loved.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your ancestors. But they came to Baal-Peor and consecrated themselves to Shame, and they became detestable like the thing they loved.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reverse reproductive sequence and the bird image without softening the loss.
verses.before: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird— no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
verses.after: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird— no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird— no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit bereavement and the speaker's departure, not a euphemism for reduced prosperity.
verses.before: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them until no one remains. Indeed, woe to them when I turn away from them!
verses.after: Even if they raise children, I will bereave them until no one is left. Woe to them when I depart from them!
verses.tsw_comparator: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them until no one remains. Indeed, woe to them when I turn away from them!

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult pinned Tyre reading and keeps the explicit killing threat.
verses.before: Ephraim, as I saw him, was like Tyre planted in a meadow, but Ephraim must bring out his children to the killer.
verses.after: Ephraim, as I saw him, was like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. Yet Ephraim must bring his children out to a killer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim, as I saw him, was like Tyre planted in a meadow, but Ephraim must bring out his children to the killer.

verses.rationale: Preserves the prophet's interrupted petition and bodily terms without supplying a consoling explanation.
verses.before: Give them, O LORD— what will you give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that are dry.
verses.after: Give them, LORD—what will you give? Give them a miscarrying womb and breasts that have dried up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give them, O LORD— what will you give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that are dry.

verses.rationale: Keeps the hard divine declarations and rulers/rebels wordplay in a clear close.
verses.before: “All their evil is at Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of the evil of their deeds I will drive them from my house. I will love them no more; all their officials are rebels.
verses.after: “All their evil was at Gilgal; there I came to hate them. For the evil of their deeds I will drive them from my house. I will love them no longer; all their rulers are rebels.
verses.tsw_comparator: “All their evil is at Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of the evil of their deeds I will drive them from my house. I will love them no more; all their officials are rebels.

verses.rationale: Preserves the movement from tree to children and the explicit first-person killing.
verses.before: Ephraim is struck; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will put to death the precious fruit of their womb.”
verses.after: Ephraim is struck down; their root has dried up, and they will bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will kill their cherished children.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim is struck; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will put to death the precious fruit of their womb.”

verses.rationale: Marks the return to prophetic third-person speech with my God unchanged.
verses.before: My God will reject them because they did not listen to him, and they will become wanderers among the nations.
verses.after: My God will reject them because they have not listened to him. They will wander among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: My God will reject them because they did not listen to him, and they will become wanderers among the nations.

verses.rationale: Retains the abundance rather than reading empty vine and keeps the parallel misuse of prosperity.
verses.before: Israel is a spreading vine; he produces fruit for himself. As his fruit increased, he multiplied altars; as his land prospered, they made beautiful pillars.
verses.after: Israel is a luxuriant vine bearing fruit for itself. As its fruit increased, its altars increased; as its land prospered, its sacred pillars grew more splendid.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel is a spreading vine; he produces fruit for himself. As his fruit increased, he multiplied altars; as his land prospered, they made beautiful pillars.

verses.rationale: Uses false for smooth/divided hearts in context, retaining the alternative in apparatus.
verses.before: Their heart is divided; now they will bear their guilt. He will break down their altars; he will destroy their pillars.
verses.after: Their hearts are false; now they must bear their guilt. He will break down their altars and devastate their sacred pillars.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their heart is divided; now they will bear their guilt. He will break down their altars; he will destroy their pillars.

verses.rationale: Preserves both the causal admission and skeptical question.
verses.before: For now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not fear the LORD. And the king— what can he do for us?”
verses.after: Now they will say, ‘We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD. And what could a king do for us?’
verses.tsw_comparator: For now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not fear the LORD. And the king— what can he do for us?”

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant making and poisonous judgment in their agricultural image.
verses.before: They speak words, swearing empty oaths, making covenants; so judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
verses.after: They speak empty words, swear false oaths, and make covenants. So judgment springs up like poison weed in the furrows of a field.
verses.tsw_comparator: They speak words, swearing empty oaths, making covenants; so judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.

verses.rationale: Retains plural calves then singular it and the rejoicing/mourning tension, with supplied mourning signaled by syntax.
verses.before: The inhabitants of Samaria tremble for the calf of Beth-Aven. Its people mourn for it, and its idolatrous priests cry out over it, over its glory, for it has departed from it.
verses.after: Samaria’s inhabitants tremble for the calves of Beth-aven. Its people mourn over it, and its priests who rejoiced over it mourn for its glory, for that glory has gone into exile.
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitants of Samaria tremble for the calf of Beth-Aven. Its people mourn for it, and its idolatrous priests cry out over it, over its glory, for it has departed from it.

verses.rationale: Matches the unusual royal epithet of 5:13 and retains counsel as the cause of shame.
verses.before: It also will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will receive shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.
verses.after: It too will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the contending king. Ephraim will receive shame; Israel will be ashamed of its counsel.
verses.tsw_comparator: It also will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will receive shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his counsel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the floating fragment image; notes foam as another rendering of qetseph.
verses.before: Samaria’s king is cut off like foam on the face of water.
verses.after: Samaria’s king will be swept away like a twig on the surface of water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samaria’s king is cut off like foam on the face of water.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aven and the paired desperate appeals rather than paraphrasing death wishes.
verses.before: The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. Thorn and thistle will grow over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall upon us!”
verses.after: The high places of Aven, Israel’s sin, will be destroyed. Thorns and thistles will grow over their altars. They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us!’ and to the hills, ‘Fall on us!’
verses.tsw_comparator: The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. Thorn and thistle will grow over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall upon us!”

verses.rationale: Reads the negative war clause as a rhetorical question while noting the difficult syntax.
verses.before: From the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel. There they have stood. Will not war against the children of injustice overtake them in Gibeah?
verses.after: “Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel. There they have remained. Will not war overtake them in Gibeah, war against the children of wrongdoing?
verses.tsw_comparator: From the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel. There they have stood. Will not war against the children of injustice overtake them in Gibeah?

verses.rationale: Follows the read offenses rather than written furrows/eyes possibilities and leaves the two offenses unidentified.
verses.before: When I desire, I will discipline them, and peoples will be gathered against them when they are bound for their twofold guilt.
verses.after: When I wish, I will discipline them. Peoples will gather against them when they are bound for their two offenses.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I desire, I will discipline them, and peoples will be gathered against them when they are bound for their twofold guilt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unusual passing over the neck rather than silently adding sparing; distinguishes all three agricultural tasks.
verses.before: Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, and I passed over the beauty of her neck. I will make Ephraim carry a rider; Judah will plow; Jacob will harrow for himself.
verses.after: Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, but I passed over her beautiful neck. I will harness Ephraim; Judah will plow; Jacob will harrow for himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, and I passed over the beauty of her neck. I will make Ephraim carry a rider; Judah will plow; Jacob will harrow for himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps the extended field imagery and rain/teach ambiguity for the closing verb in a note.
verses.before: Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap according to steadfast love. Break up for yourselves fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD until he comes and rains righteousness upon you.
verses.after: Sow righteousness for yourselves; reap a harvest of faithful love. Break up your unplowed ground. It is time to seek the LORD until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap according to steadfast love. Break up for yourselves fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD until he comes and rains righteousness upon you.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned your way rather than emending to chariots and preserves the contrasting harvest.
verses.before: You have plowed wickedness; you have reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of falsehood. Because you trusted in your way, in the multitude of your warriors,
