verses.after: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. You trusted in your own way, in your many warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have plowed wickedness; you have reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of falsehood. Because you trusted in your way, in the multitude of your warriors,

verses.rationale: Preserves the named but uncertain historical allusion and actual violence against families.
verses.before: tumult will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated, as Shalman devastated Beth-Arbel on the day of battle, when mother was shattered upon children.
verses.after: The uproar of battle will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated, as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.
verses.tsw_comparator: tumult will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be devastated, as Shalman devastated Beth-Arbel on the day of battle, when mother was shattered upon children.

verses.rationale: Keeps Bethel as source's subject and the emphatic duplicated destruction verb, without adding an invader.
verses.before: Thus he will do to you, Bethel, because of your great evil. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
verses.after: This is what Bethel has done to you because of your immense wickedness. At dawn Israel’s king will be utterly cut off.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus he will do to you, Bethel, because of your great evil. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named collective child and historical Egypt reference without inserting a later quotation's application.
verses.before: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
verses.after: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural unnamed callers rather than silently changing the verb to I called.
verses.before: The more they called to them, the more they went away from them. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
verses.after: The more they called to them, the more they went away from them. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned offerings to carved images.
verses.tsw_comparator: The more they called to them, the more they went away from them. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.

verses.rationale: Reads the difficult his-arms phrase with Ephraim as referent and preserves the caregiving and plural shift.
verses.before: Yet I was the one who taught Ephraim to walk; I took them by their arms, but they did not know that I healed them.
verses.after: Yet I was the one who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms. But they did not know that I healed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I was the one who taught Ephraim to walk; I took them by their arms, but they did not know that I healed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pointed yoke rather than repointing infant; preserves the singular ending within the tender animal image.
verses.before: I drew them with cords of humanity, with bonds of love. I was to them like one who lifts a yoke from their jaws, and I bent down and fed them.
verses.after: I drew them with human cords, with ropes of love. I was to them like one who lifts a yoke from their jaws; I bent toward him and fed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I drew them with cords of humanity, with bonds of love. I was to them like one who lifts a yoke from their jaws, and I bent down and fed them.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned negative despite tension with other Egypt sayings and repeats return with changed direction.
verses.before: They will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria will be their king, because they refused to return to me.
verses.after: He will not return to the land of Egypt; Assyria will be his king, because they refused to return.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria will be their king, because they refused to return to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps bars as a concrete reading of baddim and records alternatives rather than overidentifying counselors.
verses.before: The sword will whirl in their cities, consume their bars, and devour because of their counsels.
verses.after: The sword will whirl through his cities, consume his gate bars, and devour because of their schemes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sword will whirl in their cities, consume their bars, and devour because of their counsels.

verses.rationale: Renders the extremely compressed upward/rise wording cautiously and flags other parses in the note.
verses.before: My people are bent on turning away from me. Though they call them upward, no one at all will raise them up.
verses.after: My people are bent on turning away from me. Though they are called upward, no one rises at all.
verses.tsw_comparator: My people are bent on turning away from me. Though they call them upward, no one at all will raise them up.

verses.rationale: Preserves four questions, both destroyed-city names, and the internal turning of the divine heart.
verses.before: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart turns within me; all my compassion grows warm.
verses.after: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah or treat you like Zeboiim? My heart turns within me; all my compassion grows warm.
verses.tsw_comparator: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart turns within me; all my compassion grows warm.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned city wording in the disputed final clause; notes wrath reading without substituting it invisibly.
verses.before: I will not carry out the fierceness of my anger. I will not again destroy Ephraim, for I am God and not a human being, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.
verses.after: I will not unleash my burning anger; I will not turn to destroy Ephraim again. For I am God, not a man, the Holy One among you. I will not enter a city.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will not carry out the fierceness of my anger. I will not again destroy Ephraim, for I am God and not a human being, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps the lion now as summons and renders from sea geographically as west.
verses.before: They will walk after the LORD. He will roar like a lion; when he roars, children will come trembling from the west.
verses.after: They will follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will walk after the LORD. He will roar like a lion; when he roars, children will come trembling from the west.

verses.rationale: Preserves both nations and the repeated trembling/bird imagery now in restoration.
verses.before: They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their houses,” says the LORD.
verses.after: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from the land of Assyria. I will settle them in their homes,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their houses,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult wandering verb and holy plural as divine designation; notes the opposing faithful-Judah interpretation.
verses.before: Ephraim has surrounded me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still wanders with God, and with the Holy One who is faithful.
verses.after: “Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit. Judah still wanders with God, with the faithful Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim has surrounded me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still wanders with God, and with the Holy One who is faithful.

verses.rationale: Preserves destructive east wind and both political transactions without adding motives.
verses.before: Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the east wind all day. He multiplies falsehood and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.
verses.after: Ephraim feeds on wind and chases the east wind all day. He multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria and carry oil to Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the east wind all day. He multiplies falsehood and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and oil is carried to Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah and Jacob distinct in the lawsuit and reciprocal repayment.
verses.before: The LORD has a case against Judah and will attend to Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.
verses.after: The LORD has a case against Judah. He will call Jacob to account for his ways and repay him for his deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has a case against Judah and will attend to Jacob according to his ways; according to his deeds he will repay him.

verses.rationale: Retains heel-grasping wordplay and the paired stages of Jacob's life.
verses.before: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his strength he struggled with God.
verses.after: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel; in his strength he struggled with God.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his strength he struggled with God.

verses.rationale: Keeps ambiguous he/him and the striking us instead of harmonizing the line with Genesis.
verses.before: He struggled with the messenger and prevailed; he wept and sought favor from him. At Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us—
verses.after: He struggled with an angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us—
verses.tsw_comparator: He struggled with the messenger and prevailed; he wept and sought favor from him. At Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us—

verses.rationale: Retains both divine-name occurrences and the memorial-name sense.
verses.before: the LORD, the God of Hosts; the LORD is his memorial name.
verses.after: the LORD, the God of Armies; the LORD is the name by which he is remembered.
verses.tsw_comparator: the LORD, the God of Hosts; the LORD is his memorial name.

verses.rationale: Renders the instrumental with/by God as help while preserving love, justice, and waiting.
verses.before: So you, return to your God; keep steadfast love and justice, and wait continually for your God.
verses.after: So return with your God’s help. Keep faithful love and justice, and wait continually for your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you, return to your God; keep steadfast love and justice, and wait continually for your God.

verses.rationale: Uses merchant for Canaan while preserving its ethnonym wordplay in a note.
verses.before: A merchant has deceptive scales in his hand; he loves to oppress.
verses.after: A merchant has dishonest scales in his hand; he loves to exploit.
verses.tsw_comparator: A merchant has deceptive scales in his hand; he loves to oppress.

verses.rationale: Keeps the speaker's self-exonerating claim rather than endorsing it.
verses.before: Ephraim says, “Surely I have become rich; I have found wealth for myself. In all my labor they will find in me no guilt that is sin.”
verses.after: Ephraim says, ‘I have become rich; I have gained wealth for myself. In all my earnings they will find no guilt in me, nothing that is sin.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim says, “Surely I have become rich; I have found wealth for myself. In all my labor they will find in me no guilt that is sin.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the terse Egypt formula and festival/tent association without deciding return to exile versus wilderness in text.
verses.before: Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again as in the days of the appointed festival.
verses.after: But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of the appointed festival.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again as in the days of the appointed festival.

verses.rationale: Keeps three modes of communication and renders similitudes accessibly.
verses.before: I spoke to the prophets; I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I gave parables.
verses.after: I spoke to the prophets; I multiplied visions. Through the prophets I gave comparisons.
verses.tsw_comparator: I spoke to the prophets; I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I gave parables.

verses.rationale: Maintains the Gilead/Gilgal/heaps sound cluster in named terms and concrete stones.
verses.before: If Gilead is wickedness, surely they will become nothing. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars will become like heaps of stones beside the furrows of a field.
verses.after: Is Gilead wickedness? Surely they have become worthless! At Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars too will be stone heaps in the furrows of a field.
verses.tsw_comparator: If Gilead is wickedness, surely they will become nothing. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars will become like heaps of stones beside the furrows of a field.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jacob/Israel alternation and twice-repeated wife as the reason for service.
verses.before: Jacob fled to the field of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he guarded sheep.
verses.after: Jacob fled to the countryside of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he tended flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob fled to the field of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he guarded sheep.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed prophet and guarding link with Jacob's flock work.
verses.before: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was guarded.
verses.after: Through a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt; through a prophet Israel was guarded.
verses.tsw_comparator: By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was guarded.

verses.rationale: Renders bloods as bloodguilt and retains adonaw as his Lord rather than adding YHWH.
verses.before: Ephraim provoked bitter anger; so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and return his reproach upon him.
verses.after: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger. His Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim provoked bitter anger; so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and return his reproach upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserves Ephraim's former stature and abrupt death outcome.
verses.before: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal and died.
verses.after: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he stood high in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal and died.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal and died.

verses.rationale: Chooses human sacrificers rather than sacrificers of humans, explicitly noting the consequential alternative.
verses.before: And now they continue to sin. They make for themselves cast images from their silver, idols according to their understanding, all of them the work of craftsmen. They say concerning them, “People who sacrifice humans kiss calves!”
verses.after: Now they sin more and more. From their silver they make cast images for themselves, idols fashioned by their skill, all of them craftsmen’s work. Of these they say, ‘Let the people who sacrifice kiss the calves!’
verses.tsw_comparator: And now they continue to sin. They make for themselves cast images from their silver, idols according to their understanding, all of them the work of craftsmen. They say concerning them, “Those who sacrifice humans kiss calves!”

verses.rationale: Preserves all four vanishing images and matches the repeated morning/dew language.
verses.before: So they will be like the morning cloud, like dew that goes away early, like chaff blown from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a window.
verses.after: So they will be like a morning cloud, like dew that vanishes early, like chaff whirled from a threshing floor, like smoke from an opening.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore they will be like the morning cloud, like dew that goes away early, like chaff blown from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a window.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exclusive knowing and saving claims and repeated Egypt self-identification.
verses.before: Yet I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. You will know no God but me, and there is no savior besides me.
verses.after: “But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. You shall know no God except me; there is no savior besides me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. You shall know no God but me, and there is no savior besides me.

verses.rationale: Follows knew rather than alternate fed and retains the hostile landscape.
verses.before: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of burning heat.
verses.after: I knew you in the wilderness, in a land of scorching heat.
verses.tsw_comparator: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of burning heat.

verses.rationale: Repeats fullness to make the causal sequence of prosperity and forgetting clear.
verses.before: According to their pasture, they became satisfied. They were satisfied, and their heart became exalted; so they forgot me.
verses.after: When they found pasture, they ate their fill. When they were full, their hearts grew proud; that is why they forgot me.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to their pasture, they became satisfied. They were satisfied, and their heart became exalted; therefore they forgot me.

verses.rationale: Reads ashur as watching rather than the nation Assyria and retains both predators.
verses.before: So I will be to them like a lion; like a leopard by the road I will watch.
verses.after: So I will be like a lion to them, like a leopard watching beside the road.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will be to them like a lion; like a leopard by the road I will watch.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily tearing and bereaved bear imagery without reducing them to generic punishment.
verses.before: I will meet them like a bear bereaved of her cubs and tear open the covering of their heart. There I will devour them like a lioness; a wild animal will tear them apart.
verses.after: I will meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs and tear open the covering of their hearts. There I will devour them like a lion; a wild animal will rip them apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will meet them like a bear bereaved of her cubs and tear open the covering of their heart. There I will devour them like a lioness; a wild animal will tear them apart.

verses.rationale: Chooses the difficult against-me construction and notes possible question/other subject readings.
verses.before: You have destroyed yourself, Israel, for your help is only in me.
verses.after: You are ruined, Israel, because you are against me, against your helper.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have destroyed yourself, Israel, for your help is only in me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the where question and quoted demand without naming an earlier monarch.
verses.before: Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities, and your judges, of whom you said, “Give me a king and officials”?
verses.after: Where is your king now, that he may save you in all your cities? Where are your judges, of whom you said, ‘Give me a king and rulers’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities, and your judges, of whom you said, “Give me a king and officials”?

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel giving/taking and anger/fury without harmonizing tense into an ongoing cycle.
verses.before: I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my fury.
verses.after: I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my fury.

verses.rationale: Retains stored guilt imagery rather than replacing it with an abstract record.
verses.before: The guilt of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored away.
verses.after: Ephraim’s guilt is tied in a bundle; his sin is stored away.
verses.tsw_comparator: The guilt of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored away.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift from laboring figure to child and the failure to emerge.
verses.before: Pains of childbirth come upon him, but he is an unwise child, for at the right time he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.
verses.after: Labor pains come upon him, but he is an unwise son. When the time comes, he does not present himself at the opening for birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pains of childbirth come upon him, but he is an unwise child, for at the right time he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.

verses.rationale: Chooses questions in the judgment context while recording affirmative rescue reading; retains Sheol and the unsoftened final line.
verses.before: Will I ransom them from the hand of Sheol? Will I redeem them from death? Where are your plagues, O Death? Where is your destruction, O Sheol? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.
verses.after: Shall I ransom them from Sheol’s power? Shall I redeem them from death? Where are your plagues, Death? Where is your destruction, Sheol? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shall I ransom them from the hand of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from death? Where are your plagues, O Death? Where is your destruction, O Sheol? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps brothers as pinned rather than reeds and preserves flourishing-to-drought-to-plunder movement.
verses.before: Though he flourishes among brothers, an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will dry up, and his fountain will become dry. It will plunder the treasury of every precious vessel.
verses.after: Though he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come, a wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will dry up; his fountain will run dry. It will plunder the treasury of every precious object.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though he flourishes among brothers, an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will dry up, and his fountain will become dry. It will plunder the treasury of every precious vessel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete atrocity language and public verse mapping from Hebrew14:1.
verses.before: Samaria will bear her guilt, for she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little children will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
verses.after: Samaria must bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little children will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samaria will bear her guilt, for she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little children will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.

verses.rationale: Keeps return and stumbling as the book's closing recurring terms.
verses.before: Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your guilt.
verses.after: Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled in your guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your guilt.

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned bulls/lips image rather than silently substituting fruit; explains the verbal offering in a note.
verses.before: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him: “Take away all guilt; receive what is good, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.
verses.after: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him, ‘Take away all guilt and accept what is good. We will offer the bulls of our lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him: “Take away all guilt; receive what is good, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three renunciations and fatherless compassion as their grounding; warhorses makes the military context accessible.
verses.before: Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses. We will no longer say, ‘Our God,’ to the work of our hands, for in you the orphan finds compassion.”
verses.after: Assyria will not save us; we will not ride warhorses. We will no longer call the work of our hands “Our God,” for with you the fatherless finds compassion.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses. We will no longer say, ‘Our God,’ to the work of our hands, for in you the orphan finds compassion.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the returning/turning wordplay and plural-to-singular collective reference.
verses.before: “I will heal their turning away; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.
verses.after: “I will heal their turning away; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will heal their turning away; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.

verses.rationale: Keeps dew now life-giving and the unusual Lebanon root comparison without adding cedars to the text.
verses.before: I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and send out his roots like Lebanon.
verses.after: I will be like dew to Israel. He will blossom like a lily and send down roots like Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and send out his roots like Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Preserves three distinct botanical senses: growth, appearance, and scent.
verses.before: His shoots will spread; his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
verses.after: His shoots will spread; his splendor will be like an olive tree, his fragrance like Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: His shoots will spread; his beauty will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Follows the causative revive-grain form and leaves the shade's masculine referent open.
verses.before: People who dwell in his shadow will return; they will revive like grain and blossom like the vine. His remembrance will be like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.after: Those who live in his shade will return. They will bring grain to life and blossom like a vine. His renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who dwell in his shadow will return; they will revive like grain and blossom like the vine. His remembrance will be like the wine of Lebanon.

verses.rationale: Keeps a single divine speaker as one plausible reading while noting dialogue alternatives; retains tree and fruit imagery.
verses.before: Ephraim will say, “What more have I to do with idols?” I myself answer him and watch over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; from me your fruit is found.
verses.after: Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? I am the one who answers and watches over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; your fruit comes from me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim will say, “What more have I to do with idols?” I myself answer him and watch over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; from me your fruit is found.

verses.rationale: Closes with the wisdom invitation and shared paths producing opposed outcomes, without turning it into an added moral.
verses.before: Who is wise and understands these things? Who is discerning and knows them? For the ways of the LORD are right; the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.
verses.after: Who is wise enough to understand these things, discerning enough to know them? The LORD’s ways are straight: the righteous walk in them, but rebels stumble in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is wise and understands these things? Who is discerning and knows them? For the ways of the LORD are right; the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.

comparative_references.scope: All 197 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
